title: French Republican Calendar
intro: The French Republican calendar reorganises civil dates around the revolutionary year and a ten-day rhythm.
epoch: 1 Vendemiaire, Year I corresponds to 22 September 1792 Gregorian (JDN 2375840), the founding of the First Republic.
structure: Twelve 30-day months each contain three ten-day decades. Five complementary days, or six in a leap year, complete the year outside the regular months.
example: After Fructidor 30 come the complementary days; the next year begins at Vendemiaire 1.
history: Adopted during the Revolution in 1793, the calendar was officially used through the end of 1805. Month names reflect seasonal and agricultural themes.
model: The provider anchors contemporary Years I–XIV to the documented historical dates and uses a shifted Gregorian leap test on Republican year + 1 for the arithmetic continuation beyond historical use.
limits: The continuation is not the full Romme proposal, nor evidence of continued historical use. It does not make the independent French decimal clock part of this date calendar.
